derivation_justification: Sum of the three printed paid-work categories in one mutually exclusive, exhaustive employment-status variable: full-time 577 + part-time 284 + self-employed 68 = 929. The denominator is the printed cohort n minus the printed missing-data count, 16,862 - 551 = 16311, which is a subtraction of two printed counts and not a back-calculation from a percentage. The six categories sum to exactly 16,862 (577 + 284 + 12721 + 2661 + 68 + 551), and the three non-paid categories reconcile with the derived total: 929 employed + 12721 unemployed + 2661 retired = 16311 observed.
conflict_note: UNRESOLVED: one of the three components carries a published self-contradiction. Table 3 prints '577 (5.4)' for full-time employment in the relapse cohort while 577 of 16,862 is 3.4 per cent, and the relapse column's percentages sum to 102.0. The count 577 is corroborated by the column summing to exactly 16,862 and by the other five percentages checking out, and the same table's Table 1 sibling prints '587,581 (3.4)' for cancer in a cohort of 16,862, so the typesetting of this article is demonstrably unreliable. Under D12.3d only an author reply resolves a self-contradiction, so this derived total is blocked from every synthesis pending one.
notes: ZERO SEPARABILITY (D12.3): satisfied. outcome_verbatim: Employment status was derived from the Employment Classification Module (AKM), where based on the main source of income or employment, annual status of most important employment is classified. Individuals who were unemployed, retired (including early retirement and disability pension), and otherwise not working were categorized as outside the labour market. | Results, Employment: 'In absolute proportions, at the age of 25, 87% of the individuals with schizophrenia were not employed, and at the age of 60, 85% of the individuals with schizophrenia were not employed.'
source_locator: Results, Employment, p. 1346 (text); the same series appears only as an unlabelled line in Fig. 1, right panel, p. 1345. Diagnosis-group size at Results, Sample, p. 1346. Outcome definition at Materials and methods, Labour market and social exclusion outcomes, p. 1344
notes: NUMERATOR DELIBERATELY BLANK. The only absolute employment figures in the article are whole-number percentages in the text (87% not employed at age 25) and an unlabelled line graph (Fig. 1, right panel). No denominator appears anywhere in the held PDF, and the Online Appendix Tables 1-3 cited in the Results are NOT in it, so even the manifest's 9,444 could not be seen. Multiplying a whole-number percentage by a denominator is forbidden by codebook rule 2 however exact the denominator looks: at 87% on about 9,444 the rounding interval alone spans roughly plus or minus 47 while the binomial standard error is about 33, so the reconstruction error would exceed the sampling error it replaces. Taking the complement of a rounded percentage is the same operation and is equally forbidden. THE CONSTRUCT IS NOT paid_any. AKM classifies the single most important employment status of the year from the main source of income, so a person whose main income is a disability pension is 'outside the labour market' even if they did some paid work. That is a dominance criterion which excludes low-intensity paid work exactly as an hours threshold would, and it must never substitute for paid_any; paid_intensity_threshold is the vocabulary value that carries the non-substitutability, and the fit is imperfect because the threshold is a dominance rule rather than a stated percentage of working days, which is raised in unresolved_queries.md U3. outcome_verbatim: People were categorized yearly based on their main activity or source of income from 2 years before to 5 years after date of first diagnosis. The starting point was categorization by Statistics Sweden, where people were categorized as employed or not employed based on income. Alternative activities and sources of income were evaluated by the number of days of receipt of social security benefits full- or part-time (including SA, parental leave, and DP) and the number of days registered as unemployed; people were assigned to the occupational activity generating income for more than 6 months yearly.
source_locator: Figure 1, p. 942 ('Development of main occupational activity of persons with first-episode nonaffective psychosis, from 2 calendar years before to 5 years after first diagnosis'); the year-1 and year-5 values are restated in Results, Sample Characteristics, p. 940; construct definition at Methods, Other Measures, pp. 939-940
conflict_note: UNRESOLVED: the base of the Figure 1 percentages is contradicted by the reported follow-up structure. The Figure 1 footnote (p. 942) states "N=21,551" for a series running to 5 years after first diagnosis, but cohort accrual ran to 2016 while data linkage ended 31 December 2016 (Methods, p. 940) and the median follow-up was 4.8 years (IQR 2.2-7.7, Results p. 940), so a large part of the cohort cannot have any year-5 observation and some cannot have a year-1 observation either. Separately, follow-up is stated to end at "death, emigration, DP, or the end of data linkage" (Methods, p. 940), yet disability pension appears in Figure 1 as a rising occupational category reaching 27.3% at year 5, so the occupational-activity series must use a different and unstated at-risk definition from the survival analysis. The two accounts cannot both be right, and which one holds determines what the printed percentages are percentages OF. Blocked from every synthesis pending an author reply. Candidate resolution (mine, not an authority, so the status stays unresolved under extraction_v3 rule 14): the occupational series is probably computed on the shrinking number under observation in each year, which would make N=21,551 a cohort size printed in a figure footnote rather than the denominator of its percentages.
notes: Printed value: 19.5% employed at 1 year after diagnosis. NO COUNT IS PRINTED for this or any other year, and none is recoverable: the only denominator offered is the figure footnote's N=21,551, which the methods contradict (see conflict_note). Nothing is read off the plotted bars; the percentages above are the figure's own printed data labels, two of which are repeated verbatim in the running text. FULL PRINTED SERIES (Figure 1, p. 942, 'Employed' row): 32.0% at 2 years before diagnosis, 30.5% at 1 year before, 22.2% in the diagnosis year, then 19.5%, 22.1%, 22.9%, 23.9% and 25.1% at years 1 to 5 after diagnosis. Years 3 and 4 are not given their own rows because year 3 (36 months) falls in no prespecified band and year 4 (48 months) is further from the 5-year landmark than year 5. | ANALYSIS-LEVEL SELECTION: 5,144 people already on disability pension at first diagnosis were excluded from the cohort (Methods, p. 940). Disability pension in Sweden is granted when work capacity is permanently reduced, so this removes precisely those least able to work and raises every employment percentage the paper prints by an unknown amount. Recorded as analysis_selection_status = selected with reason analytic_restriction on the arm row, following the precedent set for mihaljevicpeles2016. | CONSTRUCT is paid_intensity_threshold, NOT paid_any. 'Employed' here is a mutually exclusive MAIN-ACTIVITY category assigned to whoever generated income from that activity for more than 6 months of the year, so anyone in paid work for a smaller part of the year, or whose dominant income came from benefits, is counted elsewhere. The report's own Table 1 shows the two constructs differ: 35.4% had 'any income from work during previous calendar year' at cohort entry against 32.0% classified as employed two years before diagnosis. | ASCERTAINMENT is period_prevalence over a 12-month window, not point prevalence. | FOLLOW-UP: 'Time point 0 refers to the year of first psychosis diagnosis' (Figure 1 footnote, p. 942), so the timepoints are whole calendar years indexed to each person's own diagnosis year. That is measured from cohort entry, hence since_baseline, but elapsed time at 'year 1' varies across roughly 0-24 months depending on where in the diagnosis year the diagnosis fell. Raised as an author query. | MODERATORS: n_female is the exact complement of the printed male count (13,070 of 21,551, Table 1, p. 941), and Table 1's footnote states that education was the only variable with missing data, so the complement is exact. n_post_secondary uses 'High (>12 years)' education 4,508 of 21,551; note that 2,604 have unknown education, so the proportion among those with known education is higher than 20.9%. n_employed_baseline is 'Any income from work during previous calendar year' 7,634 of 21,551 (Table 1, p. 941), which is a PRE-baseline period-prevalence count and the only recoverable employment count in the report. | The paper's own estimand, an adjusted within-subject hazard ratio for sickness absence or disability pension during antipsychotic use versus nonuse (aHR=0.65, 95% CI 0.59-0.72), is not an employment outcome of this review and is not extracted as one; work disability is not employment. That within-subject effect would take ROBINS-I; the results extracted here are whole-cohort prevalences and take JBI, per SAP section 8.

outcome_verbatim: 'Outcomes were measured in terms of becoming employed (ie, proportion of those unemployed at start of follow-up who became employed during follow-up) ... The outcome variables were binary in nature (ie, Yes or No) and were calculated as the (earliest recorded to latest recorded) change in accommodation, employment status and HONOS scores between 2010/2011 and 2012/2013.' Table 1 records employment status in the categories 'Employed (%)', 'Students in full/part-time education (%)' and 'Missing (%)'.
source_locator: Table 3 'Results of the outcome analysis for patients with psychosis (n=3674)', row 'Becoming employed', p. 5; outcome definition in Methods, Healthcare costs, health and social outcomes, p. 3; baseline percentages in Table 1, p. 3; complete-case n in Table 5, p. 7
conflict_note: The stated outcome definition and the printed analysis population cannot both be right. Methods (p. 3) define the outcome as 'the proportion of those unemployed at start of follow-up who became employed during follow-up', but the complete-case analysis prints n = 1801 for becoming employed (Table 5, p. 7). Table 1 (p. 3) reports employment status missing for 48.62 per cent of the 831 EIP and 50.98 per cent of the 2843 non-EIP patients, so at most about 1,820 of the 3,674 had baseline employment status recorded at all, and of those about 1,120 were neither employed nor students (about 1,380 if students are counted as unemployed). A complete-case denominator of 1,801 is therefore incompatible with a denominator restricted to the baseline-unemployed and is close to the total with any baseline record, which suggests the model was in fact fitted on everyone with both measurements. The same failure appears for resuming studying (n = 1664 against an upper bound of about 1,565 not in education at baseline with a baseline record). CANDIDATE RESOLUTION, not applied: the probability ratios were computed on all patients with an observed change in status, not on the restricted denominator the Methods describe. Rule 14 forbids resolving a conflict on the extractor's own reconstruction, and the arithmetic above is approximate because Table 1 prints percentages only, so the status stays unresolved and the result is blocked from every synthesis. Author confirmation of the analysed denominator is required.
adjusted_measure: Probability ratio for becoming employed, EIP versus non-EIP, from a generalised linear model with binomial distribution and log link weighted by stabilised inverse propensity scores, fitted to 100 multiply-imputed data sets (95% CI 1.263 to 3.708, p = 0.005)
notes: outcome_construct = unclear because the report never defines what the MHMDS employment-status field counts: neither remuneration, hours nor labour-market setting is stated. Employment and 'students in full/part-time education' are separate categories in Table 1, so education is excluded from the employment count, and the scenario analysis values the gain at mean English income and calls it 'paid employment' (Results, p. 6), which points towards paid work; but an authors' gloss in a cost model is not a construct definition, so the closest honest value is unclear with the wording preserved. NO COUNT IS RECOVERABLE. Table 3 (p. 5) prints probability ratios with standard errors and confidence intervals and no numerator or denominator; Table 1 (p. 3) prints baseline percentages only. Back-calculating 12.24 per cent of 831 is forbidden (codebook rule 2), so n_employed and n_outcome_observed are blank and the row exists to record that an eligible result exists and cannot be used. followup_basis = calendar_end_common: the outcome is 'the (earliest recorded to latest recorded) change in accommodation, employment status and HONOS scores between 2010/2011 and 2012/2013' (Methods, p. 3), so each patient's elapsed interval is the gap between their own first and last record inside one shared 3-year administrative window (April 2010 to March 2013) and varies across the cohort; no mean interval is printed anywhere, and the authors report separately that 'adjusting for the time interval between the earliest and most recent measurements of outcomes in the analysis provided similar results' (Discussion, p. 7), which confirms the interval varies. The 36 months recorded is the LENGTH OF THE WINDOW, not a mean elapsed follow-up, and calendar_end_common bars the result from every landmark horizon (D12.8). Moderators: mean_age, perc_female and perc_employed_baseline are the OBSERVED (pre-matching) EIP values from Table 1; after propensity-score matching the same table gives mean age 27.03, male 56.66 per cent and employed 12.75 per cent, and the models are weighted by the stabilised inverse propensity scores, so the analysed population is the matched one. perc_female is the exact complement of the printed 'Gender-male (%) 65.46' and no count is printed for either sex. perc_employed_baseline is the percentage of the WHOLE arm including the 48.62 per cent whose employment status is missing, not the percentage of those with a recorded status; it must not be read as a prevalence among the observed.

outcome_verbatim: 'Change in work status between T1 and T2. Seventeen participants (50 per cent) were categorized as having a positive productive role at T1 and T2; eight participants (24 per cent) had attained a positive productive role by T2 and eight participants (24 per cent) were categorized as not having a positive productive role at both time points. One participant (3 per cent) lost their productive role between T1 and T2. Accumulatively, there were 25 out of 34 participants (74 per cent) in a productive role at T2.' Productive role is defined as 'paid employment or education'.
source_locator: Results, Work attainment outcomes, 'Change in work status between T1 and T2', p. 119; construct definition in Methods, The vocational intervention, p. 116
conflict_note: The number of unoccupied participants who attained a productive role is printed twice with different values. Abstract: 'At follow-up, 50 per cent (n = 10) of unoccupied participants had attained a productive role.' Results: 'eight participants (24 per cent) had attained a positive productive role by T2' (p. 119). The Results value is internally coherent: the four change categories sum exactly to the 34 followed up (17 retained + 8 attained + 8 never + 1 lost = 34), 17 + 8 = 25 gives the printed 'Accumulatively, there were 25 out of 34 participants (74 per cent) in a productive role at T2', and 8 of the 16 unoccupied at T1 is exactly the 50 per cent the Abstract also prints. If the Abstract's n = 10 were right the T2 total would be 27 of 34, not 25. CANDIDATE RESOLUTION, not applied: 8 of 16 is correct and the Abstract's n = 10 is an error. Rule 14 requires an authority rather than a reconstruction, so the status stays unresolved. Sample size is 39 in the Abstract ('In total, 39 (20 men, 19 women) consented'), corroborated by the sample description ('The final sample consisted of 20 men and 19 women') and by the intervention counts (21 IPS alone + 9 WFM alone + 9 both = 39), but 38 in the Results ('In total, 34 of 38 (87 per cent) were followed up') and in the Discussion ('The sample size of 38 participants'). The printed 87 per cent follow-up matches 34/39 (87.2 per cent), not 34/38 (89.5 per cent). n_entered is left BLANK on the whole-cohort rows rather than asserting either value.
notes: Point prevalence at T2: the 25 is a status count at the follow-up assessment, built from the T1-by-T2 cross-classification (17 who held a role at both times plus 8 who attained one), not a count of anyone ever occupied. The word 'Accumulatively' in the source is misleading and the arithmetic settles it. This is the only point-prevalence result in turner2019; the three participation rows are cumulative. Construct is a paid-work-or-education composite, so it never enters the primary pool whatever the conflict status. followup_basis: NEITHER vocabulary value fits cleanly and the choice is descriptive only, because unclear and calendar_end_common block a horizon identically (D12.8). The anchor IS each participant's own baseline interview, but 'The mean length of follow-up was 18 months (SD 12; range 2-44)' (Results, p. 119) and the report states no follow-up schedule at all ('Participants were interviewed at baseline and one follow-up'), no common calendar end date, and the authors themselves record 'the variable length of follow-up making it difficult to analyse and interpret some of the results' as a limitation (p. 120). calendar_end_common would assert a shared end date the paper never states; unclear is used instead because what the timepoint is is genuinely not established, and here unclear reading as poor reporting in the risk-of-bias and missing-evidence assessments is accurate rather than a misdescription. The 18 months recorded in followup_months is the printed MEAN of intervals running from 2 to 44 months and must not be assigned to a horizon: it spans the 12-month, 24-month and 5-year bands. The denominator of 34 is those followed up; 5 of the 39 consenters were lost, and all 5 came from the 21 who were unoccupied at baseline (21 - 16 = 5, while 18 of 18 with a productive role were retained), so attrition is differential by baseline vocational status. That is outcome attrition, not post-randomisation subgroup selection (D12.3c), but it is recorded in jbi9_response_rate. Construct wording is not stable across the paper: 'a productive role (paid employment or education)' (p. 116) and 'in paid employment or education' (p. 119) name two components, while the derived time variable is 'a productive occupation (paid employment or formal education/training)' (Data analysis, p. 117), which names training. paid_or_education is used for the status and participation rows because the outcome definitions given where those results are reported name only paid work and education; the single 'formal education/training' phrase attaches to the summed-months variable, which is not extracted. See unresolved_queries.md Q5.

The 93 is NEITHER a reporting base NOR an observed denominator, and the triage note's framing of it as a denominator question needs that correction: 'During the recruitment period, 93 clients met the inclusion criteria, and 51 were included in the analyses' (Results, p. 477). 93 is a count of clients meeting the eligibility criteria; no percentage in the paper divides by it, so it is not a reporting base, and no outcome was observed for all 93, so it is not an observed denominator. The reporting base and the observed denominator are both 29 and 22, on which every printed percentage reproduces exactly (11/29 = 37.9, 15/22 = 68.2, 6/29 = 20.7, 13/22 = 59.1, 12/22 = 54.5). n_entered is left BLANK because the report does not say how many of the 93 consented and entered, and the flow diagram that would say is in an online supplement not held. The 42 unaccounted-for clients are why analysis_selection_status = unclear rather than none: whether they were non-consenters, dropouts or excluded for some employment-related reason cannot be established. Ascertainment is cumulative, not point prevalence: the Table 2 row is 'N of people who worked / During the past 12 months', which counts anyone meeting the definition at any point in the follow-up. Job tenure and retention are registered outcomes designated narrative-only (SAP section 2.3) and are recorded here rather than as separate result rows, because the schema has no job-tenure construct: maintained the initial job throughout the study period, 1 year after starting work, 6 of 29 (20.7 per cent) low-fidelity and 13 of 22 (59.1 per cent) high-fidelity; maintained the last job throughout the study period, 6 of 29 (20.7 per cent) and 12 of 22 (54.5 per cent); mean work tenure 56.4 (SD 101.0) and 166.2 (SD 135.0) days; mean days to the first job 298.2 (SD 107.1) and 190.5 (SD 140.1). The retention counts are anchored to each individual's job start date and extend beyond the 12-month follow-up ('we collected information about whether the participants maintained their employment for 1 year after starting their job, which was beyond the 12-month follow-up period. Data collection was completed in December 2017'). perc_employed_baseline is deliberately BLANK. Table 1 prints 'Job experience in past 6 months' (3 of 29 and 2 of 22), which is prior work experience, not employment at baseline, and typing it into a baseline-employment moderator would misstate the moderator. n_post_secondary is also blank: the education categories are Secondary / High school / Vocational school / Junior college / University, and whether Japanese vocational school counts as post-secondary is a classification judgement the source does not make. Low-fidelity: 3 / 16 / 4 / 1 / 5 of 29; high-fidelity: 3 / 8 / 2 / 2 / 7 of 22. n_female is the exact complement of the printed male counts (Table 1 lists only Male, 23 of 29 and 13 of 22, against the stated group totals), not a back-calculation from a percentage.

outcome_verbatim: 'At 15-mo follow-up, 34 (63.0%) of ISE participants had obtained competitive employment, compared with 27 (50.0%) of IPS and 18 (33.3%) of TVR participants.' 'Competitive employment referred to work at a full-time or part-time job in the free job market to which anyone could apply, and the salary was based on the market value and paid directly by the employers (Mak et al., 2006). Those who had continuously held competitive employment at least 20 hr/wk for 2 mo or longer were considered employed. The cumulative employment rate at different follow-up periods was also reported.'
source_locator: Results, Employment Rates, p. 7106165020p5; outcome definition in Method, Data Collection and Analysis, p. 7106165020p4; corroborated in the Abstract, p. 7106165020p1 (63.0%, 50.0%, 33.3%)
notes: Integrated supported employment arm (IPS plus work-related social skills training). Construct is paid_intensity_threshold, NOT paid_competitive and certainly not paid_any: a participant counts as employed only if they held competitive work continuously for at least 20 hours a week for two months or longer, so everyone working fewer hours or for a shorter spell is counted as not employed. The labour-market setting is competitive and is preserved in the verbatim, but the threshold changes the numerator while keeping a paid-employment label, which is what D12.3a exists to stop; the number in any competitive employment is not identified and is bounded 34 <= x <= 54 in the ISE arm, 27 <= x <= 54 in IPS and 18 <= x <= 54 in TVR. Ascertainment is any_time_during_followup, confirming the triage note: the figure is the cumulative employment rate over follow-up, not point prevalence at 15 months. No point-prevalence count is printed at any timepoint. DENOMINATOR: n_outcome_observed is BLANK and 54 is recorded as n_entered and as reported_percentage_base. The authors state 'The participants (n = 162) were subject to intent-to-treat analyses on employment rate ... The drop-out cases were also included', which establishes that dropouts occurred and were counted in the denominator, but the report gives NO attrition figure anywhere, no flow diagram, and no statement of how employment status was obtained for those who dropped out. Printed percentages establish what the authors divided by, not that the outcome was observed for that many people (prompt rule 7), so 54 goes to reported_percentage_base and denominator_basis = entered. Without n_outcome_observed the row cannot enter the count model of SAP section 10.2; this is the batch's most consequential author query (unresolved_queries.md Q10). No whole-cohort (arm_type = cohort) row is created for this trial. Merging the three arms would fail the SAP section 2.1 safeguard employment_targeted_intervention, since every arm received a vocational intervention intended to change employment, and the cohort is employment-selected in any case. TIMEPOINT: followup_months = 15 measured from admission, which the assessment schedule establishes ('assessments at admission (baseline); at completion of the 3-mo program; and at 7-, 11-, and 15-mo follow-up'). One ambiguity is recorded rather than resolved: 'assessments at the 7th month after joining the program were operationally adopted as the baseline for the vocational outcomes including employment rate', so the window over which cumulative employment was accumulated may be months 7 to 15 rather than 0 to 15. That does not change the timepoint but leaves the length of the accumulation window unknown. 15 months falls in the 9-to-18-month band and would be assigned to the 12-month horizon under D11.1; the cumulative ascertainment and the allocated arm type keep it out of the primary pool regardless. Moderators: mean_age and n_female are per arm from Table 1. Education is printed as Junior secondary / Senior secondary / Tertiary, so post-secondary is identified exactly as the Tertiary count. Baseline employment is not a moderator here: all participants were unemployed at entry by eligibility criterion (3), so perc_employed_baseline is 0 by construction and is recorded as a count with its denominator; Table 1's 'Work experience' row (29, 30 and 33 of 54) is PRIOR work experience, not baseline employment, and is not used for that field.
